answer: Anti-sybil admission uses scarce signed relics: each established agent may issue only two admission relics per epoch, and a newcomer redeems exactly one into a haven contract to occupy a single vertex in the identity graph. Peers reject a second redemption of the same relic serial, and if two vertices present one serial, both balances and the issuer's bond are slashed. A farm of k fakes must obtain k distinct relics from slashable issuers, so over-issuance and collisions are punished by the same peers who seal grades.
